claim: 75 Hard was created by Andy Frisella: basically a challenge, if you will, described by him as "a tactical guide to win the war with yourself"
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In a lot of ways, winning the war with yourself, as in 75 Hard, is what this show is all about
Not having done Andy Frisella's specific 75 Hard challenge before, and already doing a lot of it daily, the decision was to do it and kind of amp it up
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: There seem to be some important ways to do 75 Hard in a Holistic Alpha style
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: The basic rules of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created them
A basic rule of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created it: follow a diet for the entire 75 days, with zero alcohol and zero cheat meals
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Andy Frisella doesn't get specific about which diet to follow in 75 Hard: the idea is that you must follow a specific eating plan
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: A basic rule of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created it: two 45-minute minimum workouts each day, at least three hours apart, one of which must be done outside regardless of the weather
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: A basic rule of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created it: drink a gallon of water a day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: A basic rule of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created it: read at least 10 pages a day of a nonfiction self-improvement, self-development, growth-related type of book
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: A basic rule of 75 Hard, as Andy Frisella created it: take a progress picture each day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: You can read a lot more about 75 Hard and sign up for free: Andy Frisella's website sends the details, but it's pretty simple
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Andy Frisella also has a podcast episode that goes into more detail on 75 Hard, and sells a book that goes into a little more
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Really most of 75 Hard was already daily. Rarely a cheat meal anymore, or anything you'd call one, from no motivation for it: the preference is to eat what feels good. Typically two training sessions a day, though not necessarily every single day before, and certainly during the challenge. Usually a gallon of water, and usually a progress pic, now made sure of every day for the 75. The reading is a little new: a lot of audiobooks, but to follow the spirit of the challenge, a paper book, at least ten pages
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: The Holistic Alpha way of 75 Hard, suggested if you want to try it: the five basic rules plus three additions
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: An addition in the suggested Holistic Alpha way of 75 Hard: zero ejaculations for the 75 days
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: An addition in the suggested Holistic Alpha way of 75 Hard: at least one meditation every day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: An addition in the suggested Holistic Alpha way of 75 Hard: a cold shower every day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In 75 Hard, if you fail on any one of the items, you start over at day one, the way Andy Frisella lays it out and the way suggested here too: no cheat days, 75 straight days
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: You can adapt 75 Hard to you personally
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: If there's more you want to add on top of the 75 Hard minimums you can, but you don't have to
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Do at least the minimums Andy Frisella lays out for 75 Hard: there's a reason they're there
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: A personal version of 75 Hard, ramped up to make the idea Andy Frisella lays out applicable personally, to where things stand: all his rules plus the three additions, tracked with tallies (a tally app already used daily for the important self-care items and some other things), with a few added. Most were already tracked daily. All of it every day for at least the next 75 days
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, two cold showers a day: usually one morning and one evening already, now a daily thing
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, a gallon of water a day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, meditating twice a day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, at least five rounds of Wim Hof breathing, made part of the challenge after trying to implement it on a more regular basis
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: If you haven't heard of Wim Hof breathing, look up Wim Hof and the Wim Hof breathing method

In the personal version of 75 Hard, on top of the two 45-minute workouts, daily minimums on specific exercises: 350 burpees, 350 push-ups, 350 squats, 150 arm haulers or Supermans (basically bodyweight back work), 35 pull-ups, and at least eight sprints
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, at least two Kegel training sessions a day
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, edging at least once a day: not necessarily every day before, but the benefits are felt when doing it
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, at least 10 pages of a self-development book, and the progress picture
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, a podcast episode every day through the 75 days, not all about the challenge, each with a minute of update on staying on track and the previous day's numbers, to stay accountable
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, Lumosity, a brain-training app, personally found to make a difference in the brain
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, a target for how much content gets produced online

claim: In the personal version of 75 Hard, time to roll out the body and do some fascia release, definitely needed with those fitness numbers
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Some of you are probably already doing a number of the 75 Hard things: some of you already get a couple of training sessions a day, maybe you already drink that amount of water

claim: Take wherever you are and go for 75 Hard, give it a shot

claim: If you haven't really been working out or following a specific eating plan, maybe do the basics of 75 Hard
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: 75 Hard is called 75 Hard for a reason: it's not easy, and for a lot of people it is a major, major challenge
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: The basics of 75 Hard had been part of daily life for a long time, so things had kind of moved a little beyond them already, hence the ramp-up
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: You don't need to ramp up 75 Hard as much, but the suggestion is to do the basics of the Holistic Alpha way, which is really three key additions to the normal program
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: The Holistic Alpha way of 75 Hard is not easy, but guaranteed, if you put it into action you will see some changes
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: Excited to put the ramped-up 75 Hard into action, and it will definitely be a challenge to keep up some of the specific workout numbers and accomplish everything, having ramped it up quite a bit from the basics
name: 75 Hard challenge

claim: The numbers on day three of the 75 Hard challenge: two cold showers, a gallon of water, two meditations, five Wim Hof breathing rounds (the minimum), 400 burpees (minimum 350), 430 push-ups (minimum 350), 150 arm haulers, 400 squats (minimum 350), 40 pull-ups (a little over the minimum), eight sprints, two 45-minute-plus workouts, both actually outside, two Kegel sessions, an edging session, the 10 pages read, the body rolled out, the podcast happening right then, Lumosity, a progress picture, and the content goals met. "Forward, we shall move"
name: 75 Hard challenge
